beats.note: Encryption is used throughout everyday computing.
One of the most familiar examples is HTTPS, which protects communication between a web browser and a website.
When a website uses HTTPS, information such as login credentials, personal details, and payment information is encrypted while traveling across the internet.
Encryption is also used in messaging applications.
End-to-end encryption is designed so that a message is encrypted on the sender’s device and decrypted only on the recipient’s device.
Ideally, even the messaging provider cannot read the contents of the message while it is in transit.
Another major application is data storage.
Computers, smartphones, USB drives, and cloud services can encrypt stored files.
This is called encryption at rest.
If a device is lost or stolen, encryption can make it much more difficult for someone to access the information stored on it.
